sophia: Heads up: saw regression in 2/4 Dedicated clusters. p50 unchanged, p99 for mixed-tenant workloads jumped from ~420ms -> ~1.6s. Seems correlated with high KV cache churn and a few long-sequence requests forming huge batches that block short requests. Profiling attached.

perf-ci-bot: perf-ci uploaded artifacts: https://perf/internal/2054321122/flame.svg and timeline: https://perf/internal/2054321122/timeline.html

mike: @sophia do we have kernel selection metrics? are long sequences pulling kernels that preempt others? :thinking:

sophia: Yes — kernel-hotpath logs show repeated kernel reinitialization when a long sequence enters batch with different max_seq. Also batching trace shows batch-formation waits up to 180ms for long requests to fill. KV cache hit rate for those tenants drops from 82% -> 54% during spikes.

anya: That's the classic head-of-line problem. Two quick ideas: (1) dual-queue: short-lane cap (tokens<=64) that gets fast-path and strict cap on per-tenant queued short tokens, (2) aging score so older short requests escalate priority.

kevin: Agree. Also thinking of per-tenant dynamic token reservation: allocate a small reserve 'short_token_budget' per tenant that replenishes slowly; spare capacity can be borrowed. Should prevent starvation without reducing throughput.

jasmin: What about KV cache eviction? If long sequences cause many kv writes/evictions, hits for short ones drop and they need to recompute KV, lengthening service time.

sophia: Good point. I measured eviction churn: hotset churn rate up 3x when long sequences dominate. Proposed experiment below.

sophia: ```
experiment:
  name: short-lane-reserve+aging-v1
  rollout: 10% nodes
  configs:
    short_token_threshold: 64
    short_lane_capacity: 64   # max short slots per batch
    per_tenant_reserve_tokens: 128
    reserve_refill_rate: 4/s
    aging_boost: 10  # priority points per 500ms wait
    kv_eviction_policy: lru-weighted-hotset
metrics:
  - p50_latency
  - p95_latency
  - p99_latency
  - kv_hit_rate
  - batch_fill_wait_ms
  - fairness_index (short_vs_long_p99_ratio)
```

mike: Nice. Can we add kernel-selection guard: if incoming request's seq_len > batch_median*2 then route to separate kernel instance (or batch size cap) to avoid kernel reboots?

kevin: We can. But need to ensure capacity for that path. Maybe set fallback policy: if fast-path backlog > X, allow borrowing.

sophia: I'll push experiment to 10% tomorrow morning and add tracing hooks. Asking @mike @kevin to review the perf harness patch. I'll also include a small synthetic mix to reproduce locally: 80% short (16-64 tokens), 20% long (512-2048).

mike: I'll take the harness review. If local reproducer looks good I'll run full cluster sim.

jasmin: Also tagging eng-sre for alert threshold adjustments — p99 spike should trigger runbook earlier. @eng-sre :eyes:

runtime-bot: runtime-bot scheduled experiment rollout to 10% at 2025-06-04T09:00Z (ticket #INF-712).

anya: :rocket: keep changelog in experiment ticket with perf plots. small wins first.

mike: ack — will report back with waveform and KV hit traces.
